notes.title: Voice of the Deep Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/2040a2b2824d59ef5123f68b065cb557fafbd36c.jpg[/img]

The Precursors built this place to contain something. Something interested in you. The Voice of the Deep update is now available on Steam! Learn more on the [url=https://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/voice-of-the-deep]Voice of the Deep site[/url].

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vtsyXKSmBWE

The Voice of the Deep Update introduces big pieces of Subnautica’s end-game. The mystery surrounding many story arcs is finally revealed!

[h1]The Containment Facility[/h1]

Deep beneath the ocean floor, a huge Precursor facility lies embedded in the rock. Inside explorers will find a multitude of artefacts, data repositories, and fragments of history.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/49110ec77112cca3faa6ae2a8293509aed491e63.jpg[/img]

[h1]Emperor Leviathan[/h1]

The Containment Facility contains… Something. That something is massive, and very much interested in you. The Emperor Leviathan might be a friend, a foe, or neither: We recommend you exercise caution when entering the Containment Facility.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/2040a2b2824d59ef5123f68b065cb557fafbd36c.jpg[/img]

[h1]Silent Running 2.0[/h1]

We’ve listened carefully to your feedback, and made a second pass on Cyclops Silent Running. The Cyclops has been enhanced with stronger shields, larger energy reserves, and new abilities. The engine may now be shut down for complete silence, giving you a safe haven from which to operate. 

The boat may be rigged for silent running at any speed. After activation, the Cyclops will be silent for a short time, while the ability regenerates. High speed dashes are possible with flank speed, but watch out, the engine might overheat if you run at flank speed for too long.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/6725671c93b02647396bd17ca337af468f43985b.jpg[/img]

[h1]Precursor Pipes[/h1]

Mysterious pipes have appeared throughout the world. They appear to be both ingesting and discharging large volumes of water and… Peepers. What is the purpose of these pipes? Why are the Peepers swimming through them? It is a mystery for intrepid divers to solve!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/4c7cd4ef23f34841c251d148d1fddb85a31edb10.jpg[/img]

[h1]New PDA Interface[/h1]

The Personal Digital Assistant (PDA) has received a glorious overhaul. A slick new interface acts to provide you with detailed information about undersea flora and fauna. Better yet: Icons throughout the game have received a makeover, too. Subnautica has been rolling with placeholders for a long time. No more!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/07ad537ad10222875187cd08c2922ad4d26835bc.jpg[/img]

[h1]Lifepod 7[/h1]

A new stricken Lifepod is available for you to find and explore. Lifepod 7 contains eclectic treasures for any diver clever enough to find it!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/d8a03acd0b8b4fd794ec59274729238c608af233.jpg[/img]


[h1]Bulb Zone & Ghost Forest Teleporters[/h1]

Two new teleporters may be found, one in the Bulb Zone and one in the Ghost Forest. Where do they lead?

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/7a767d488ec5da8938b9c6ccf731b1833eaf4461.jpg[/img]

[h1]Get Development Updates[/h1]

Be notified the moment we release the next Subnautica Update, by subscribing to the [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]Subnautica Development Newsletter[/url] and following [url=https://twitter.com/subnautica]@Subnautica on Twitter.[/url]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710

notes.title: Subnautica Silent Running update adds submarine stealth and much more
notes.content:
A few days ago, undersea survival game Subnautica received a humdinger of an update that added a new Silent Running mode to your aquatic exploration pod. This plays into one of the update's other big features: dangerous creatures that are newly interested in your previously safe Cyclops vessel. You'll need to enable Silent Running mode to deal with them, which turns off all exterior lights, replaces interior ones with an eerie red glow, and slows your pod the heck down, so you can sneak past those aggressive undersea monsters.

Other new features include a revamped Cyclops UI, a terrain-scanning sonar update, creature-detection on the HUD, and the ability to launch creature-distracting decoys. If the Cyclops vessel has been a harbour of refuge for you from the scary deep, you might be a little concerned to hear that it's just been made more fragile—it can even end up wrecked if it takes too much damage.

"Not only do creatures take an interest in your machine," the extensive update post explains, "but once damaged, the Cyclops can become wrecked. Take precautions necessary to mitigate emergencies onboard your ship. Luckily, Fire Extinguishers now have fancy wall holsters to aid in your firefighting. Use the Holographic Status display to monitor for damage and fires. Once the Cyclops reaches hull strength of zero, it will become wrecked. It can be salvaged for materials used in building add-ons later, but the machine itself can no longer be repaired or deconstructed".

You can read the full details of the update here.

notes.title: Silent Running Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/7fdca75f72d7109220fd5c10adf3e0369cfebdb3.gif[/img]

A huge Cyclops Submarine overhaul has arrived: The Silent Running Update. Visit the dedicated [url=https://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/silent-running]Update Site[/url] to see it in action.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JuFoil12HzI

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/b3350ff0e7f443d81552bbd8ed5158d6c03c1bc6.jpg[/img]

[h1]Red Alert: Fire detected![/h1]

Look out: Aggressive creatures can now damage the Cyclops. They will tear holes in the hull, and if enough damage accumulates, fires will start. Extinguish the fires quickly, or risk losing the boat!

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/b6395829ba2fd689137001e8ab94eb8d19645129.jpg[/img]

[h1]Rig for Silent Running[/h1]

The Cyclops now has multiple operating modes: Ahead Slow, Ahead Standard, Ahead Flank, and Silent Running. Each represents a different tradeoff between speed travelled and output of light and noise. The noisier and brighter your Cyclops runs, the more likely it is to be attacked by aggressive creatures.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/2074864372e4f5208beeadc9226f04a128c84e40.jpg[/img]

[h1]Sonar Contact[/h1]

Two new sonar modules are available for the Cyclops. First: A Terrain Scanning active sonar that reveals the contours of the sea-bed ahead. Second: A Threat detecting passive sonar that displays the location of hostile creatures around the submarine.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/756f339d1b06bfdb547c1f202885657fe1d618ab.jpg[/img]

[h1]Raise Shields[/h1]

You are not helpless in the face of creature aggression. Raise shields to temporarily deflect incoming attacks. Deploy decoys to distract aggressive creatures while you pass. And activate the Fire Suppression System to extinguish fires that burn beyond control.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/e5518b4b137604f6897167829456da40801bf72f.jpg[/img]

[h1]Abandon Ship[/h1]

A fatally damaged Cyclops will experience hull failure - Killing anyone caught inside. Get off the boat while you still can! Once the wreck settles on the ocean floor, you can swim inside to salvage upgrade modules and equipment.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/8575562b91dbd35d9fe75df0629cf1e1ea80a497.jpg[/img]

There's lots more to the Silent Running update. Check out the [url=https://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/silent-running]Silent Running update website[/url] to see more!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/Subnautica/

There's lots more to the Silent Running update. Check out the [url=https://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/silent-running]Silent Running update website[/url] to see more!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/Subnautica/

tags.feature: Look out: Aggressive creatures can now damage the Cyclops. They will tear holes in the hull, and if enough damage accumulates, fires will start. Extinguish the fires quickly, or risk losing the boat!

The Cyclops now has multiple operating modes: Ahead Slow, Ahead Standard, Ahead Flank, and Silent Running. Each represents a different tradeoff between speed travelled and output of light and noise. The noisier and brighter your Cyclops runs, the more likely it is to be attacked by aggressive creatures.

Two new sonar modules are available for the Cyclops. First: A Terrain Scanning active sonar that reveals the contours of the sea-bed ahead. Second: A Threat detecting passive sonar that displays the location of hostile creatures around the submarine.

You are not helpless in the face of creature aggression. Raise shields to temporarily deflect incoming attacks. Deploy decoys to distract aggressive creatures while you pass. And activate the Fire Suppression System to extinguish fires that burn beyond control.

A fatally damaged Cyclops will experience hull failure - Killing anyone caught inside. Get off the boat while you still can! Once the wreck settles on the ocean floor, you can swim inside to salvage upgrade modules and equipment.

notes.title: Castles & Coffee Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/ee2c99a2e7a71ae567143c7d0a5dd8769163d9b1.jpg[/img]

A new Subnautica Early Access Update has been released! Prepare to dodge Lava...

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6qRYTWxRdsw

[h1]Lava Castle Precursor Base[/h1]

A secret lies hidden deep within the bowels of the Lava Castle: A Precursor Base. Great peril awaits any diver attempting to explore this mysterious structure. A [b]Sea Dragon Leviathen[/b] guards the entrance, [b]Stalkers[/b] prowl the narrow lava passageways, while immense heat and pressure threaten near certain death.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/de12917e16b890048f67a1b821de2ff075a87f71.jpg[/img]

If you can make it inside, treasures and secrets await.

[h1]Ion Power[/h1]

The ocean is vast, and often inhospitable. Your survival depends on maintaining a steady supply of power to your equipment and vehicles.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/dd100ef241274107c88e75b04679d0a6e3467d2d.jpg[/img]

New "Ion" batteries and power cells are much longer lasting than existing power sources. Their extended run times allow you to conduct more exploration work between charges.

[h1]Coffee Machines[/h1]

Occasionally we add a feature to Subnautica that really matters. A feature of great consequence. The coffee machine is one of those features. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/7c20f8022f1e39d66ec013ec9e38849eb807617b.jpg[/img]

Find the coffee machine amongst the wreckage of the Aurora, place it in your base, and bask in the glory of having achieved greatness.

[h1]Gravsphere[/h1]

The Gravsphere pulls in everything around it. Deploy a Gravsphere to draw in predators, prey and loot. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/964a94d680d327808dc132fdc1ae2942eba7d953.jpg[/img]

We've been experimenting with prototypes of the Gravsphere for some time. The Castle's and Coffee Update brings the Graveshere's proper model and animations.

[h1]Luggage Bags[/h1]

The luggage bag acts as portable storage. Pick it up, put it down, and store items in it.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/133d4125da7d171877c9cf9e4e4d06113e3dd5a7.jpg[/img]

Like the coffee machine, the luggage bag may be found in the wreckage of the Aurora.

[h1]Working Trash Cans[/h1]

Alright, stick with us for a moment. This is important. Trash cans actually work. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/5ab8d8071ae6f388b962c8250123dce9d4898bbe.jpg[/img]

Say goodbye to inventory clutter: Trash cans mean you can throw stuff away. It's not exactly environmentally friendly, and we don't know where the stuff goes, but this is the future so don't worry too much about it.

[h1]Air Bladder[/h1]

The Air Bladder now has a proper model and animations. Use the Air Bladder to rapidly ascend to the surface. Useful in sticky situations where you need to get to get up from the depths, fast!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/4b8f610bf817fa936594bebdbb26715c30c7ab28.jpg[/img]

[h1]Skip Time[/h1]

You can now advance time by sleeping.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/a46ac96404c753ab55899c92162c7e55c3d0f427.jpg[/img]

Find the night time too spooky? Hit the hay when the sun sets and you will wake up to the sun shining through your sea-base windows.

[h1]Other Little Things[/h1]

[list]
[*]Halved Seaglide light energy cost
[*]Quartered Seaglide active energy cost
[*]Removed frame-rate dependence problem with Seaglide energy usage
[*]Removed Kyanite from Blood Kelp (only drillable now)
[*]Added Kynanite to recipe for 3rd stage of the rocket (resource sink)
[/list]

[h1]Follow Subnautica Development[/h1]

[list]
[*]See our active [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica-development]tasks and development plans[/url]
[*]Receive a [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]newsletter the moment we release an update[/url]
[*]Review [url=https://twitter.com/subnauticascm]changes made in real time[/url]
[/list]

[h1]Buy Subnautica[/h1]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/

notes.title: Precursor Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/e89d13b2cfab2992541760461c420836a9c38c8b.jpg[/img]

[h1]The Mysteries of Subnautica Grow Deeper[/h1]

The Precursor Update has been released! This latest update is chock full of new secrets to unravel. Previously, you may have noticed strange, high-tech cubes - or bases - placed throughout the world. Now, these unusual objects come to life as someone (or something) flips the switch. Dive deep into the story of Subnautica and discover more answers and more questions:

https://youtu.be/MKpr1zdFYk4

[h1]Precursor Base & Array[/h1]

Rising out of the ocean is the massive Precursor Array & Base. There is a lot to explore both within the new base and nearby. Be sure to bring a flashlight.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/ef49453a0f31a7ff923202a3a14fb2969fc33c90.jpg[/img]

[h1]Cave Network[/h1]

The area behind the Precursor Base is teeming with hidden gems and secret passageways. Ancient technology sits within these caves waiting to be awakened by you.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/1f8da0e97bbcc12bfbf2897e4ee7da2e3077a98c.jpg[/img]

[h1]Ancient Artifacts[/h1]

Scattered throughout the world are new Precursor story elements and clues.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/27f97f7814502bb9c64e2d053bd6639578b987ee.jpg[/img]

[h1]Biome Additions[/h1]

The Lost River and Floating Island Biomes have received a thorough level-polish.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/e1356f7882dcbece54ef580aa6f20538b977ef90.jpg[/img]

[h1]Fall Damage[/h1]

Be careful walking along cliffs, the world now has fall damage.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/1a7174732d8cb79e20fd3705a4b0913ae0d744ac.jpg[/img]

[h1]Vehicle PDA[/h1]

It's now possible to use the PDA while driving vehicles, a highly requested addition.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/4a75a8819ef5da975265cfed400b34d0509a36ac.jpg[/img]

[h1]Find Out More[/h1]

Learn more about the Precursor Update  [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/Precursor-Update]on the update feature site[/url]. We send out a newsletter every time Subnautica Early Access is updated. If you would like to receive it, sign up to the [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]Subnautica Development Mailing List[/url].

Happy diving,

- [url=http://twitter.com/uwedev]The Subnautica dev team[/url]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/

notes.title: Dangerous Creatures Update
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/c272c1a0b9981fededb0332344bcee04a417d90e.jpg[/img]

[h1]Keep one eye on the open ocean[/h1]

The Dangerous Creatures update has been released! This update includes the massive Sea Dragon Leviathan, terrifying Warper, Crab Squid EMP blasts, the Reinforced Dive Suit, a new Abandoned Base, and more:

https://youtu.be/Xe2XutnTjC8

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/ff7c8fea250964b09f72afb1ec5668e95bf9c56b.jpg[/img]

[h1]Sea Dragon Leviathan[/h1]

The massive Sea Dragon Leviathan may be found in Lava biomes: It spews fireballs, crushes creatures with its huge jaws, and bats aside anything in its path with enormous claws.

If you see a Sea Dragon: [b]Swim.[/b]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/1162d493a4d54c111409de752b88e776d7a0d4ac.jpg[/img]

[h1]Warper[/h1]

Appearing out of nowhere, the Warper teleports in and out of almost any biome. This creature is extremely dangerous and indiscriminate in its attacks on other lifeforms - Including you.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/9622b44b22febd30285011f692860d6405d983d5.jpg[/img]

[h1]Abandoned Base 3[/h1]

The third and final abandoned base may be found in the Grand Reef biome. Search the base for clues as to what happened on this ocean planet before the Aurora crashed. But watch out, there are Crab Squids about...

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/23f849187e4fc74cba57c199faca1f814f71ad9c.jpg[/img]

[h1]Crab Squid Electromagnetic Pulse[/h1]

Crab Squids may now deploy an electromagnetic pulse (EMP) attack. The pulse disables electronics, such as flashlights, and may leave explorers like yourself vulnerable to attack!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/b899c64af419d2c0e6c0bd8b084f60d292290cd1.jpg[/img]

[h1]Tree Cove[/h1]

A gorgeous new environment is available for you to explore: The Tree Cove. Found within the Lost River biome, the Tree Cove is a haven of peace and tranquility, filled with gentle Ghost Rays. It's a great place to go to escape from all the new dangerous creatures prowling around!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/c2f8cd3c270a83597a3315906728ec95afd52840.jpg[/img]

[h1]Reinforced Dive Suit[/h1]

Lava Zones are very, very hot. To hot, in fact, for a regular-suited diver to survive. The new Reinforced Dive Suit allows you to explore very hot areas. Just the kind of areas the Sea Dragon is likely to inhabit...

[h1]Find Out More[/h1]

Learn more about the Dangerous Creatures Update  [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/dangerous-creatures]on the update feature site[/url]. We send out a newsletter every time Subnautica Early Access is updated. If you would like to receive it, sign up to the [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]Subnautica Development Mailing List[/url].

Happy diving,

- [url=http://twitter.com/uwedev]The Subnautica dev team[/url] :welder::mac:

notes.title: PRAWN Update Released!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/ebd9509e9dfa2690a6a2a4b79d8a84fe14e00e8e.jpg[/img]

[h1]This suit can handle the pressure.[/h1]

A brand new vehicle is available in Subnautica: The Pressure Re-Active Waterproof Nano Suit, or PRAWN Suit. This big bipedal mech-suit is yours to command, available now on [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/]Steam[/url]. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s_IuAapLVYc

The PRAWN suit is capable of diving to great depths, allowing you to explore dangerous caverns and lava fields. PRAWN comes standard with a claw arm that can be used to smash small rocks and pick up items. The suit also accepts modular arm attachments:

[list]
[*]Drill Arm: Collect resources from large resource deposits 
[*]Grappling Arm: Fires a grapple to reel in small objects, and pull the suit towards large objects. 
[*]Torpedo Launcher: Fire torpedoes to defend yourself against aggressive creatures 
[*]Propulsion Cannon: Lift, attract, and launch small and medium sized objects  
[/list]

Like the Seamoth Submersible, the PRAWN suit may be docked with a Moon Pool or Cyclops Submarine for repairs, recharging, and modification.  

[h1]Aurora Wreckage Expanded[/h1]

Also included in the PRAWN Update: Brand new sections of the Aurora, ready for you to explore. There are a multitude of story points and items to be found amongst the wreckage.  

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/5647945/eedd5c04217d13b4cae3c924a4f8a70970980887.jpg[/img]

Find out more on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/prawn-update]PRAWN Update website[/url]. Write us a comment below and let us know what you think of the update! 

- [url=https://twitter.com/uwedev]Unknown Worlds[/url]

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/

notes.title: (Micro) Update 67
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/07/20160706_SN_Update67_Image_1-1024x576.jpg[/img]

Update 67 is now available on Steam. We haven’t named this update, because it is a little baby update. Unlike Farming, Power Nap, Machinery, and other updates, 67 doesn’t include any big exciting new features. It does include important and useful improvements to the game. Read on to find out what’s inside.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/07/20160706_SN_Update67_Image_2.jpg[/img]

Subnautica now supports the use of Xbox controllers when playing on PC. You can adjust controller bindings in a new options section in the main menu. Controllers do not yet work in the main menu itself – Sorry about that, we intend to remedy this in future.

notes.title: Power Nap Update
notes.content:
[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/06/20160601_SN_PowerNap_Hero_1080.jpg]

The Power Nap Update has been released on Steam! Check out the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/Subnautica/power-nap-update]Power Nap Update[/url] site to see all the juicy, energising details about what’s included.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=79ZxlyU2w7Q

Recharge your batteries using the new Battery Charger. The Battery Charger can be used to recharge exhausted batteries for flashlights, light arrays, and more.

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/rechargerbattery-1024x640.jpg]

Have depleted powercells as well? You can also create Powercell Charger for all your powercell charging needs.

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/rechargerpowercell-1024x640.jpg]

Time to rest your weary head on your new bed. Three options for beds make all your Habitat dreams come true. Complete with laying-down animation.

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/bed1-1024x640.jpg]

Follow around Gasopods and pick up their gas orbs as materials for the new gas torpedo. Once you have some gas pods and titanium, head over to the Seamoth upgrade station to make your torpedoes. These missiles release a cloud of toxic gas upon impact.

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/gastorpedo3-1024x640.jpg]

Sea Treaders are Subnautica’s gentle giants. As they tread along, they drop basalt rocks and (sometimes) manure. The latter can be used for bio-energy!

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/seaTreaders-1024x640.jpg]

You’ve seen them around but not like this — Introducing the final model for the Solar Panels! Just when you thought solar energy couldn’t get any better.

[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/solarpanel-1024x640.jpg]

Want to be notified next time Subnautica receives a big update? Sign up to the [url=http://eepurl.com/LhdP5]Subnautica Mailing List![/url] You can also follow development on [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica-development]Subnautica’s Trello Board[/url]. Leave us feedback by pressing F8 in game, and by posting comments below. Thanks for playing, and happy diving!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710

notes.title: Machinery Update
notes.content:
[img=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/map_2-1024x640.jpg]

A new update for Subnautica has been released! Check out the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/Subnautica/machinery-update]Machinery Update[/url] site for more. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qRjICSP7n2c

The latest and greatest technology in the world of Subnautica is the Map Scanner room. These rooms can be built on to existing habitats, or can stand alone. Map Scanner rooms will scan nearby seafloor, searching for a select array of resources. Additionally, there are two exterior cameras that can be piloted remotely. Upgrades bring additional benefits. 

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/map_1-1024x640.jpg]

The Cyclops gets a massive technology overhaul. Improvements include better proximity sensors, a hull camera, deeper dives, functioning lockers, and more. 

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/cyclops_1.jpg]

Bio Reactors and Nuclear Reactors are officially an option. Bio Reactors require plant matter to function, Nuclear Reactors require Radiation Rods [CHECK]. Both must be places in a Multi-Purpose Room. 

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/nuclear_reactor_alt-1024x640.jpg]

Thermal Reactors have been around for a while, but now they look the part. The Machinery Update brings a model to this useful piece of tech.

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/thermal_reactor_2-1024x576.jpg]

The Blood Kelp biome grows with the addition of the Blood Kelp 2 zone. Both Blood Kelp areas will serve as entrances to the Lost River Biome, still in development. In Blood Kelp 2 you will also find a new critter, the Crabsquid. Be careful not to touch, as it can deliver a nasty attack. 

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/crabsquid-1024x581.jpg]

The floating storage container now functions! Build it and fill it with all your favorite things. 

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/float_stor_2-1024x576.jpg]

Creatures will now respawn after being killed by another creature or the player. This feature was in high demand by you, the players! Thank you for your continued feedback to support the development of Subnautica.

[img= http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/05/creatures-1024x576.jpg]
Want to be notified next time Subnautica receives a big update? Sign up to the [url=http://eepurl.com/LhdP5]Subnautica Mailing List![/url] You can also follow development on [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica-development]Subnautica’s Trello Board[/url]. Leave us feedback by pressing F8 in game, and by posting comments below. Thanks for playing, and happy diving!

notes.title: Oculus Update Released
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/20160405_SN_OculusUpdate_Header.jpg[/img]

A new Subnautica update is available on Steam! The Oculus Update brings support for Oculus Rift SDK 1.3, which is a nerdy way of saying: You can play Subnautica on your Oculus Rift right now! If you already own Subnautica on Steam, it is not necessary to buy again on Oculus Home. [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=356516956]You can use your Steam copy to play with the Oculus Rift.[/url]

The Oculus Update is not just about the Oculus. There are also a bunch of new features available to everyone. First up: The main menu now has a fancy new water background. Who doesn’t like some ambient water visuals to start their game off right?

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/20160405_SN_OculusUpdate_Menu.jpg[/img]

Power is now required for Seabase Oxygen, which applies to not just Seabases, but also the Seamoth and Cyclops. If any of the three are underpowered, they will stop producing enough. Oxygen for survival. It is now crucial to ensure everything is properly powered.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/20160405_SN_OculusUpdate_BasePower.jpg[/img]

You can now sit! You’ve been hard at work on your feet since the beginning, it’s high time you take a load off and enjoy sitting in your base. In short, you can now interact with chairs. Even better, you can access your PDA while sitting. This is particularly useful as it allows you to browse your PDA without worrying about Food or Water depleting.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/20160405_SN_OculusUpdate_Chair.jpg[/img]

Reaper Leviathan, Reefback, Stalker, Bone Shark and Bladderfish are all ready for their close ups. We’ve done a lot of work on the animation of these creatures to make them move throughout the world much more nicely. Next time you see one, go in for a closer look. Well, as much as you dare.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/20160405_SN_OculusUpdate_Stalker.jpg[/img]

Last but not least, fragments will now spawn mostly within wrecks. Sometimes, they can be found elsewhere but the best place to hunt them down will be within wrecks.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/04/xbox_iter2.00_05_27_41.Still006.png[/img]

To be notified when the next major Subnautica update is released, sign up to the [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]Subnautica mailing list[/url].

notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/03/20160315_SN_CrashSequence_lifepod_repair_01-583x365.jpg[/img]

Subnautica Early Access has always featured the Life Pod – An escape capsule ejected from the crashed Aurora Starship. How did it come to rest on the ocean surface? What happened on the way down? This small update answers that question. See details about what is included in the update on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/crash-sequence]Crash Sequence site.[/url]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qptyqKkeaJQ

The Crash Sequence starts with ejection from the stricken Aurora. To experience it, start a new game of Subnautica. The game used to start with a simple fade up from black. You will find that now, the opening is a little more intense!

This small update answers that question. See details about what is included in the update on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/crash-sequence]Crash Sequence site.[/url]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qptyqKkeaJQ

The Crash Sequence starts with ejection from the stricken Aurora. To experience it, start a new game of Subnautica. The game used to start with a simple fade up from black. You will find that now, the opening is a little more intense!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710

notes.title: Space-Octopuses s Garden: Subnautica Farming Update
notes.content:
The most important things in the world, we all know, are swimming in the great outdoors, admiring flora and fauna, and caring for plants. Subnautica [official site] already had most of those covered as it dunked players onto an ocean-covered alien world to explore, build bases, and survive, and now it’s expanded flora-fancying too. Along the journey through Early Access, the Farming Update has added horticulture for scientific, nutritional, and decorative purposes in growbeds and pots. Subnautica’s plants are gorgeous, so I’ll be delighted to plant my own alien garden.

… [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Farming Update Released!
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_Header_720-618x348.jpg[/img]

A brand new Subnautica update is available on Steam! This is the Farming Update, and it allows you to build underwater farms. To see what's inside, check out the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/farming-update]Farming Update site.[/url]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M_wmfMiXjlI

New "Grow Boxes" can be used inside or outside sea bases. Over twenty-five different seed types can be placed in these boxes. Flowers, fruits, vegetables, trees, and even some plants that will try to kill you...

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_InternalGrow_720-618x231.jpg[/img]

Seeds can also be planted in a variety of pots - Both on the floor of bases, and on the walls. Using pots, you can decorate sea bases with all sorts of greenery. Compartments can also be decorated with 'Living Walls' - lush green panels.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_WallPlants_704-618x347.jpg[/img]

LED Lightsticks are a great new way to light up areas while exploring. While held, a Lighstick illuminates the area around you. When placed on the seabed, the Lighstick can light up wide areas.

[img]http://d3roov4t80dbfx.cloudfront.net/img/20160226_SN_Farming_LightStick_Poster.jpg[/img]

Night time can now be made a little less scary - Near your base, at least. Use Floodlights and Spotlights to illuminate areas around bases. Don't forget to replace floodlight batteries!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_NightLights_1280-618x323.jpg[/img]

Spotlights will automatically track nearby predators. This is a great way to avoid being ambushed by Stalkers at night!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_Stalkers_1280-1-618x323.jpg[/img]

The Farming Update introduces abandoned bases. These relics of unknown earlier explorers can be found scattered around the world. Explore abandoned bases and scan their contents to discover new technology!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_AbandonedBases_1280-618x323.jpg[/img]

Lots of creatures and plants can be stored in new Large Aquariums. These giant modules take up almost an entire large compartment. If you build them inside two stacked compartments, they will act as a glass floor for the upper level. Enter a Large Aquarium by building a hatch on the glass. Once inside, you can plant seeds and release captive creatures.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/02/20160222_SN_FarmingUpdate_LargeAquarium_1280-1-618x323.jpg[/img]

Want to be notified next time Subnautica receives a big update? Sign up to the [url=http://eepurl.com/LhdP5]Subnautica Mailing List![/url] You can also follow development on [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica-development]Subnautica's Trello Board[/url]. Leave us feedback by pressing F8 in game, and by posting comments below. Thanks for playing, and happy diving!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/

notes.title: A Flood of Dead Bugs
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/01/floodlight-1.jpg[/img]

Some Subnautica updates are flashy, fancy, and full of fantastic features. Some of them are a little more low key, delivering subtle changes and improvements. Today, we’ve released an update of the latter kind. There is one new feature: the Flood Light. Otherwise, it’s chock full of dead bugs.

The Flood Light is a new craft-able item, added by [url=http://twitter.com/sewlek]Andi[/url]. When placed, it will illuminate a large area. You might find it particularly useful for illuminating work areas around Seabases at night. After the Aurora explodes, search for a Flood Light fragment in amongst the wreckage that flies out and lands on the sea floor.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/01/floodlight2.jpg[/img]

Elsewhere, [url=http://twitter.com/max_mcguire]Max[/url] has made a significant graphical improvement. Previously, lots of objects in the game were reflecting a Safe Shallows environment, no matter what biome they were actually in. Now, scenes appear more cohesive. He are two examples. First, a Seamoth in a Kelp Forest:

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/01/seamoth.jpg[/img]

And second, a Seabase in a Grand Reef:

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/01/seabase.jpg[/img]

The full list of bugs squashed in this update is far too long to post here. There are over fifty of them, and you can see them all on the [url=https://trello.com/b/eLEWpq3P/subnautica-playtesting]Subnautica Playtesting Trello board[/url]. Go there, and then scroll to the 'Fixed & Tested Jan Patches' list. Feast your eyes on the bug gore!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2016/01/trello.jpg[/img]

The [url=https://trello.com/b/eLEWpq3P/subnautica-playtesting]Playtesting board[/url] is a great place to keep up to date on what issues are known, and being worked on. If you spot a problem not listed on the board, please let us know about it! Then, we can sink it in a future Subnautica Early Access update.

Happy diving!

- [url=http://twitter.com/hugh_jeremy]Hugh[/url]

notes.title: H2.O Update Released!
notes.content:
[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_BeforeAfter_1280.jpg[/img]

Here is the water you have always wanted! The H2.O update completely overhauls the graphics in Subnautica Early Access: new surface water, longer draw distances, richer colors, pitch black night-time, even solar eclipses! See it in action on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/h2o-update]H2.O update website[/url]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P8dbemOAwkU

The entire ocean has received a makeover. H2.O is not just a set of tweaks: [url=http://twitter.com/max_mcguire]Max[/url] has rebuilt whole chunks Subnautica's graphics rendering system. Almost everywhere you swim, you will find a new look inviting you to explore.

Subnautica's day night / cycle is now vastly more striking. Multiple moons interacting with a bright star in different ways throughout the day. Here is the ocean surface at sunrise:

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_DawnAtSurface_NoLogo_Blog_1280.jpg[/img]

H2.O is not just a pretty face. The new Scanner can provide information about technology fragments, and organisms in the ocean environment. 

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_Scanner_1280.jpg[/img]

The scanner will record its findings into the PDA. Refer to the PDA Data Bank for information about flora and fauna you find throughout the ocean.

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_PDAData_1280.jpg[/img]

The Fabricator will no longer spit out a bunch of cubes, no matter what you tell it to build. A large variety of items now have proper 3D models, making fabrication a much more fun (and less confusing!) experience.

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_Fabrication_1280.jpg[/img]

Story voiceovers are now displayed via text on the HUD, making it easier to catch dialogue you may have missed, or play the game with no sound*.

*Don't do this, [url=http://twitter.com/sy1k1]Simon[/url] will cry.

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_Subtitles_1280.jpg[/img]

Charlie has added the ability to turn Seamoth headlights on and off. This is possibly the most overdue feature in the history of video games.

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_SeamothLights_1280.jpg[/img]

During H2.O, we tracked over two hundred 'pieces of work' on our development team Trello board. A huge number of changes have been made to Subnautica. This update is probably our biggest since 'Seabases' back in early 2015. Head on over to [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]the Trello board[/url] and look at the 'H2.O Done' column to see what we did.

[img]https://d1toq7a0ac2kyi.cloudfront.net/img/20160114_SN_H2O_Trello_1280.jpg[/img]

The H2.O update also ties together two features that were released during its development: The [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VHwcORmJJNk]Water Filtration Machine[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LJpWHO0SQLY]Aurora Wrecks[/url]. To learn more about the H2.O update, visit the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/h2o-update]H2.O website[/url], created by [url=http://twitter.com/acwjones]Andrew.[/url] To get notified about future Subnautica updates, subscribe to the [url=http://eepurl.com/LhdP5]development mailing list.[/url]

Happy diving!

- [url=http://twitter.com/hugh_jeremy]Hugh[/url]

notes.title: Shocking Update Released
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_ShockerPair-618x348.jpg[/img]

We’ve got some Shocking news – A new update is available for Subnautica Early Access! It’s called ‘Shocking,’ and it will download automatically to your Steam library. Some say that combining amps with seawater is dangerous. We say it’s a recipe for having lots of fun! Fun as in… being electrocuted. By a giant sea snake.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fyAhPYCyoRU

Shockers can be found in Koosh Zones and Blood Kelp forests.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_Shocker_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

That’s right, Blood Kelp forests. These creepy deep-ocean arboretums are as friendly as they look – But they do contain some sweet, juicy blood-sac loot. Good luck in there!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_BloodKelp_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Seaglide has always felt like it was missing something. Ever since release, the round thingamajig on its dorsal panel looked like a big blue piece of unfinished business. Now, it has been upgraded to realise its true potential! A 3D map of the surrounding sea-floor will appear hovering above your personal water craft.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_SeaglideMap_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

What is a Seaglide adventure without happy snaps? Find some sweet glowing cave system? Pics or it didn’t happen. Press F11 to take photos in game, and then review and organise them in the new PDA photo gallery.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_PictureFrame_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Photos you take in game can be uploaded to Steam. That’s nice, but sharing photos with real people is nowhere near as good as using them as decorations for your underwater home. The new Picture Frame can be built inside Seabases, and will display images from your PDA photo gallery.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_Volume_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Simon’s sound work is pretty… ‘Sy1k.’ Despite that sy1kness, it is sometimes nice to lower music and sound effect volumes. Until now that hasn’t been possible in Subnautica because Early Access. The Shocking Update brings volume controls to the in-game pause menu!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_StoryNotes_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

It’s now possible to review story points inside the PDA. Jump into the new Log section, and hear messages predicting imminent cascading dark matter quantum flux core meltdown disaster explosions!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/11/20151105_SN_ShockingUpdate_StoryNotes_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Seamoth Update Released!
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150908_SN_SeamothUpdate_Header_169_Small1-618x348.jpg[/img]

A brand-spanking new Subnautica update has been released: Seamoth! It is available right now on Steam, and will automatically download to your Steam Library if you have Subnautica installed. The best place to see what’s inside is the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/seamoth-update/]Seamoth Update page,[/url] where you find all sorts of juicy details! Hint: Torpedoes, electromagnetic pulses, armour plating…

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3Y88Z8KkMfI

The Seamoth Update brings gobs of love to the Seamoth Submersible. Almost everything in the update is centered around making the Seamoth more useful, interesting, and fun to play with. At the heart of all the goodness is the Seamoth upgrade panel, which may be found on the port side of the hull.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_upgradePanel-618x348.jpg[/img]

This panel facilitates the installation of various new upgrades. For example, Vortex Torpedoes. The Seamoth may now be configured with up to four torpedo tubes, each of which can hold four torpedoes. The ordinance is non-lethal, and designed to trap a dangerous life-form in a vortex of swirling water long enough for our intrepid protagonist to escape, pass, or do whatever needs to be done in the area.

[img]http://cloud-4.steamusercontent.com/ugc/431573231368244635/B8FD617FFA9F89F6F7569452ABA3AD19FCF5F34D/[/img]

Vortex Torpedoes are effective against lone or closely clustered lifeforms. They’re not much use if your Seamoth is surrounded by predators. Enter the electromagnetic perimeter defense module. Activating this module sends a non-lethal burst of electromagnetic radiation into the surrounding water, scaring off all but the largest ocean predators. Be cautious though, every activation drains the Seamoth battery to a significant degree.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_electricalDefense-618x348.jpg[/img]

These defensive capabilities will come in handy when exploring deep-ocean cave systems. Finding such cave systems just got a whole lot easier, thanks to the Seamoth Sonar module. This module sends out a sonic pulse, and displays the returned echo as a three dimensional mesh on the Seamoth head-up-display.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_sonar-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Seamoth is good for getting a diver from place to place. It can now move a diver’s stuff from place to place too! Storage modules may be installed to facilitate the carriage of supplies, equipment, and material.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_storage-618x348.jpg[/img]

Also available are hull re-reinforcement, battery expansion, solar array, and armour plating modules. All these modules allow the Seamoth to be configured for a wide variety of different missions. Going cave exploring? Pack food in a storage compartment, sonar, electromagnetic defense, and an extended battery. Searching for resources in an area with lots of hostile creatures? Load torpedoes, and fit empty storage compartments to carry the loot.

It gets better. Seamoths can now be customised using the new Upgrade Console. Install the console in a Moon Pool attachment point, and then use it to modify your Seamoth colour scheme and name.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_Console-618x348.jpg[/img]

A fancy, upgraded Seamoth will be a very useful companion for exploring the newly re-worked ‘Jellyshroom’ cave system. This striking network of caverns is teeming with life and exudes eeriness.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/09/20150910_SN_SeamothUpdate_Caves-618x348.jpg[/img]

There’s so much more to the Seamoth Update than is contained in this post. Check out the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/seamoth-update/]Seamoth Update Site[/url] to see more goodies like birds, mountain ranges, and some really creepy new caves.

To receive a newsletter when the next Subnautica update is released, [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]sign up to the development mailing list.[/url] Keep tabs on what the development team is up to by [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]visiting the production tracker.[/url] See every little change we’ve made to Subnautica by visiting the [url=http://subnautica.unknownworlds.com/#/subnautica/checkins]checkin and changes list.[/url] Most of the development team is on Twitter, and we are always happy to chat. Find our @handles on the [url=https://twitter.com/Subnautica/lists/subnautica-dev-team/members]Subnautica dev-team list.[/url]

notes.title: Sealab 2015: Subnautica s Habitat Update
notes.content:
I’ve had Subnautica [official site] for a while now, but only got around to installing it this weekend. As it continues to ascend out of Steam Early Access, the undersea explore ‘em up has spat out a big update with a few things that made me want to dive in. For starters, undersea bases can now have all the cool glass corridors and viewing domes that really set off a seahome look. On top of that, it’s got an eerie new reef biome hundreds of metres down, and I do dig unearthly dark waters.

Best of all: you can put a little fish tank in your base to keep pet fish.

notes.title: Subnautica's Habitat Update lets you build your own underwater lair
notes.content:
Subnautica, to make use of someone else's reductivity, is basically underwater Minecraft, but even though it's still an Early Access game, Ian liked it quite a bit in his preview. And he (and we) will probably like it even more now that the Habitat update is out, because now players can actually build a base on the bottom of the sea, complete with large rooms, panoramic observatories, and even a moon pool. 

A moon pool!

Alas, that isn't quite as cool as I first thought it would be. As Wikipedia explains, moon pools are openings in the floors of marine vessels or underwater installations that provide access to the water in a calm and protected environment. In the case of Subnautica, the moon pool serves as a dry-dock for the Seamoth submersible—practical, but still something of a letdown.

The moon pool, glass-bubble observatories, and generic "large compartments" can be strung together with standard and glass corridors as well as vertical connectors, giving completed bases a look that falls somewhere between BioShock and Habitrail. Compartments have eight attachment points for connecting corridors, dive hatches, windows, and other base modules, and can also be customized (a little bit) with wall-mounted lockers, signs, and even an aquarium.

The update also brings with it a new Biome at the 200-450 meter depth, which includes unidentified flora, resources, and danger. Details on all of it, plus a cool little interactive demonstration of how habitat flooding works, are on the Subnautica Habitat Update page.

notes.title: Habitat Update Released
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0009_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_12_showpiece-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Habitat Update is now available! Build an underwater home with Moon Pools, Observatories, large compartments, bulkhead doors, and more. Head over to the [b][url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/habitat-update]Habitat Update website[/url][/b] to see all the new features in action, or stay on this page to see an update video, and screenshots. Viewing this page inside Subnautica? Click 'view on Steam' to see images and video.

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6USpYf6Y47c

Steam will automatically download the Habitat Update. Don't have Subnautica in your Steam library yet? [b][url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710]Get a copy in the Steam Store[/url][/b]:

http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0016_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_6_moon-pool-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Moon Pool is the new king of sea-base components. This massive structure can be used to dry-dock a Seamoth submersible. The Moon Pool can be customised to your preference with reinforcements, windows, and multiple attachment points for corridors.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0018_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_4_observatory-low.jpg[/img]

Subnautica features a diverse array of unique, beautiful underwater biomes. Thanks to the new Observatory, it is now possible to enjoy the view from the safety of a sea-base.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0001_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_20_compartment-exterior-618x348.jpg[/img]

Large compartments provide lots of interior space. They include eight attachment points for the connection of corridors, dive hatches, windows, reinforcements, and other base modules.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0000_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_21_compartment-interior.jpg[/img]

Large compartments can be stacked, and ladders built between their decks.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0002_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_19_locker.jpg[/img]

Small lockers are a new storage option. They can be placed on sea-base walls, and feature a customisable label on the door.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/08/small__0008_20150805_SN_Habitat_Album_13_signage-moon.jpg[/img]

Speaking of labels, it is now possible to create customised base signage. Use the builder tool to place a label, and then enter any text. Labels can be various sizes, have arrows, and include different background options.

notes.title: OSX Update Released
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_Header-618x348.jpg[/img]

Subnautica now runs on Apple OS X! [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/]Get it now on the Steam Store[/url] - Buy it once and play on both Windows and OS X computers. Already own Subnautica for Windows? You can now play on OS X as well. The OSX Update also includes two epic new ocean biomes: Underwater Islands and Sparse Reef.

[img]http://cloud-4.steamusercontent.com/ugc/37500755696472535/2E7E384CB11248A4B9306F657F73C6757EDCDE6F/[/img]

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_FloatingIslands1_small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Underwater Islands features massive rock formations suspended above the ocean floor. Giant creatures, larger cousins of the Floater, act against the force of gravity. Bone Sharks and other creatures swim among cascades of sand.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_FloatingIslands2_small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Sparse Reef brings a new relaxed aesthetic and feel.  The blooming colors and dense features of other biomes are replaced by more earthy tones, and rolling dunes. Watch out for Bleeders…

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_SparseZone2_small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Sparse Reef also features some new fauna to discover.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_SparseZone1_small-618x348.jpg[/img]

New in the OSX Update is the Repulsion Cannon – A workbench modification of the Propulsion Cannon. The Repulsion Cannon can push large creatures and objects away. This is very useful when trying to navigate past aggressive life forms like Stalkers.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/06/20150619_SN_OSXUpdate_repulsionCannon_small-618x348.jpg[/img]

The OSX Update also features a wide array of subtle improvements to Subnautica. For example, Jonas has repaired a problem that was causing objects to pop in and out of the world inappropriately, and Andi has solved some issues with the Repulsion Cannon introduced in the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/alterra-science-update-released/]Alterra Science update.[/url]

Explore the fall range of changes in OSX Update by visiting the [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]Subnautica Trello board.[/url] You can also get a granular, all-encompassing view of the update by visiting the [url=http://subnautica.unknownworlds.com/#/subnautica/checkins]Checkin & Changes List.[/url] Keep an eye on both those spots over the coming weeks to see us build towards some big additions to sea-base building in the near future…

notes.title: Alterra Science Update
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_3_Small1-618x348.jpg[/img]

Crashed on an alien world? Surrounded by ocean predators and hostile environments? Fear not, brave traveller: For you now have new means of crafting at your disposal. The Workbench and Propulsion Cannon will transform the way you explore the ocean!

[img]http://cloud-4.steamusercontent.com/ugc/39750083270248268/A976866B3704C03660E926D87BBA8A9AF9DCE263/[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bGOSan1aip4

The propulsion cannon was developed by a crack team of Alterra Corporation scientists. The cannon may or may not exploit un-patented work by one Dr Eli Vance, an employee of one of Alterraís competitors, Black Mesa Corporation. We canít be sure. We can be sure that thanks to the propulsion cannon, the wait for Half-Life 3 is over.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_7_Small1-618x348.jpg[/img]

The propulsion cannon can be used to grab, push, drag, fling, and manipulate most smaller objects in the ocean. It definitely does not use gravity to do this.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_4_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

The new Workbench opens up new crafting and equipment customization possibilities. Build one with a Builder tool after analyzing a Workbench Fragment.

[img]http://cloud-4.steamusercontent.com/ugc/39750083270242055/FD98FF3D639087E1F82EA2F6FF2185411B3FF800/[/img]

Equipment including the Knife, Tank, and Fins can be altered using the Workbench. For example, a Knife can be modified to feature a super-heated blade. This new Heat Knife can then be used to instantly cook fish unfortunate enough to be killed by its blade.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_8_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Perhaps the most important feature of the Alterra Science update is the development of a hitherto unimaginable technology: Working doors. Run up to a Cyclops submarine door or hatch to know true science fiction futurism.

[img]http://cloud-4.steamusercontent.com/ugc/39750083270313648/22127D620768C355D8F224F712F494679F93B250/[/img]

Ever wished you could mark a cave entrance for future exploration, but canít tell all your beacons apart? Alterra Science has a super scientific solution to this problem: Beacon labels. Use them to keep track of all your stuff, and places to visit!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_5_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Seabases and the Cyclops submarine have received major visual upgrades in Alterra Science. New internal lighting gives them a slick new look.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_1_Small1-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Cyclops is not just prettier, it is also getting more clever. Alterra Science new science to submarine technology, with an upgrade console that can grant your boat greater diving depth, a stronger hull, and more.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_6_Small-618x348.jpg[/img]

Of course, as always, we canít fit everything weíve done into this blog post. Alterra Science is packed with bug fixes, tweaks, and tricks that all add together to make Subnautica Early Access a more enjoyable experience. Check out the [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]Subnautica Trello board[/url] and the [url=http://subnautica.unknownworlds.com/#/subnautica/checkins]Checkin & Changes List[/url] to see absolutely everything that went into the update!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/05/20150525_AlterraScience_2_Small1-618x348.jpg[/img]

notes.title: New Loot System
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/02/small-618x348.jpg[/img]

[i]Originally posted by [url=http://twitter.com/flayra]Charlie (Flayra)[/url] on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/new-loot-system-tech-tree-design/]Subnautica development blog.[/url][/i]

If you’ve been playing the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=355026171]Experimental branch[/url] of Subnautica on [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/]Steam Early Access[/url] this week, you may have noticed that the entire loot system and crafting tech tree have been reworked. I wanted to write something quick detailing the what and why of these big changes.

There were a few basic problems I wanted to solve:

[list]
[*]It wasn’t clear for players where to find a particular type of loot. Sometimes this was due to the loot being in too many different places or because the loot element itself was abstract or overly-scientific (Carbon, Membrane, Rutile, etc.). Players would see what elements they need in the crafting menu, but then have no idea where to find it.
[*]Many recipes were very similar or even exactly the same.
[*]Loot was too plentiful, making the loot not feel particularly “special”. It also didn’t feel as much like you were really looking for loot, it was more like you were stumbling upon it.
[*]The tech tree wasn’t very scaleable to very big recipes like the Cyclops. In order to build a Cyclops, you had to very carefully juggle your inventory or drop everything that wasn’t directly used for it in order to build it. It was clumsy and it didn’t scale to even bigger recipes for the future. It also made storage more necessary and a bit tedious.
[*]There tech tree didn’t go very deep, so there weren’t enough advanced elements. This meant that deeper areas wouldn’t have special elements or rewards for dealing with the increased light, oxygen and creature danger therein.
[*]Many of the intermediate craftable elements had only one use, which tried to justify how ingredients transformed, but added extra busy work and no choices for the player.
[*]We want to support buried or embedded loot as well, which means we need a design that allows drilling for advanced materials.
[*]Creature loot (and therefore, creatures) weren’t very relevant.
[/list]

All of these problems have existing pretty much since the first prototype, but it was just good enough to keep going forward with. But now, after we’ve ironed out so many of the game’s other bigger problems, it was time to do a proper design pass on the whole tree holistically.

I know this looks/is complicated, but a Gliffy diagram is the best I could come up with:

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/02/LootSmall.jpg[/img]
[url=http://www.gliffy.com/go/publish/7224075]Full image available on Gliffy[/url]

Here’s a summary of the biggest changes:

[list]
[*]I removed as many “abstract” elements that I could. These are elements that are generally not clear to players where they could be found. This includes Carbon, Membrane, Rutile, Zinc, Calcite, Dolomite, Flint, Emery and Calcium, among others.
[*]Loot elements are now put in the world primarily in one and only one place (“coral walls in safe shallows”) to make it clear to players where they must go if they want something. This also means that old areas won’t become obsolete as the player plunges downward. Precious minerals are always found “inside” something else: limestone chunks, sandstone chunks, shale chunks, etc. Anything that’s a chunk can be broken open to find a random mineral inside. Along the same lines, larger lodes of ore will be found inside the terrain in the future.
[*]I removed as many of the intermediate elements as possible. For instance, instead of making “battery acid”, you can use acid mushrooms directly to make batteries.
[*]Each piece of scrap metal can now be refined down into 2 1×1 pieces of titanium. This keeps the inventory/time cost of scrap, but lays the groundwork for “condensing” of materials. 10 1×1 pieces of Titanium can be further crafted into a Titanium ingot, which allows the loot to scale, to allow building of very big things.
[*]I added many more “advanced” intermediate loot ingredients to keep the progression unfolding but also to open up new branches. Wiring kits and computer chips are examples of opening new groups of tech.
[*]Whenever possible, I incorporated more creature loot into the tree. You can make enameled glass from Stalker teeth, Flares from “crash meal” (ewww?), etc. This is an ongoing goal, and a tricky one, but keeping the elements as specific as possible is helping.
[/list]

The [url=http://www.gliffy.com/go/publish/7224075]full tech tree and details can be found here.[/url] This is a live tech tree that I will keep updating for awhile at least).

I hope this explains some of the reasoning that went into some of the sweeping changes! Please let me know what you think here or [url=https://twitter.com/flayra]via Twitter.[/url]

[i]Editors note: This new system will be released to the normal, stable branch in the next major update. We're not sure when that will be just yet, sign up to the [url=http://eepurl.com/8xU4D]dev update mailing list[/url] to be notified when it is live.[/i]

Along the same lines, larger lodes of ore will be found inside the terrain in the future.
I removed as many of the intermediate elements as possible. For instance, instead of making “battery acid”, you can use acid mushrooms directly to make batteries.

Each piece of scrap metal can now be refined down into 2 1×1 pieces of titanium. This keeps the inventory/time cost of scrap, but lays the groundwork for “condensing” of materials. 10 1×1 pieces of Titanium can be further crafted into a Titanium ingot, which allows the loot to scale, to allow building of very big things.

I added many more “advanced” intermediate loot ingredients to keep the progression unfolding but also to open up new branches. Wiring kits and computer chips are examples of opening new groups of tech.

Whenever possible, I incorporated more creature loot into the tree. You can make enameled glass from Stalker teeth, Flares from “crash meal” (ewww?), etc. This is an ongoing goal, and a tricky one, but keeping the elements as specific as possible is helping.

notes.title: New Loot System
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/02/small-618x348.jpg[/img]

[i]Originally posted by [url=http://twitter.com/flayra]Charlie (Flayra)[/url] on the [url=http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/new-loot-system-tech-tree-design/]Subnautica development blog.[/url][/i]

If you’ve been playing the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=355026171]Experimental branch[/url] of Subnautica on [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/]Steam Early Access[/url] this week, you may have noticed that the entire loot system and crafting tech tree have been reworked. I wanted to write something quick detailing the what and why of these big changes.

There were a few basic problems I wanted to solve:

[list]
[*]It wasn’t clear for players where to find a particular type of loot. Sometimes this was due to the loot being in too many different places or because the loot element itself was abstract or overly-scientific (Carbon, Membrane, Rutile, etc.). Players would see what elements they need in the crafting menu, but then have no idea where to find it.
[*]Many recipes were very similar or even exactly the same.
[*]Loot was too plentiful, making the loot not feel particularly “special”. It also didn’t feel as much like you were really looking for loot, it was more like you were stumbling upon it.
[*]The tech tree wasn’t very scaleable to very big recipes like the Cyclops. In order to build a Cyclops, you had to very carefully juggle your inventory or drop everything that wasn’t directly used for it in order to build it. It was clumsy and it didn’t scale to even bigger recipes for the future. It also made storage more necessary and a bit tedious.
[*]There tech tree didn’t go very deep, so there weren’t enough advanced elements. This meant that deeper areas wouldn’t have special elements or rewards for dealing with the increased light, oxygen and creature danger therein.
[*]Many of the intermediate craftable elements had only one use, which tried to justify how ingredients transformed, but added extra busy work and no choices for the player.
[*]We want to support buried or embedded loot as well, which means we need a design that allows drilling for advanced materials.
[*]Creature loot (and therefore, creatures) weren’t very relevant.
[/list]

All of these problems have existing pretty much since the first prototype, but it was just good enough to keep going forward with. But now, after we’ve ironed out so many of the game’s other bigger problems, it was time to do a proper design pass on the whole tree holistically.

I know this looks/is complicated, but a Gliffy diagram is the best I could come up with:

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/02/LootSmall.jpg[/img]
[url=http://www.gliffy.com/go/publish/7224075]Full image available on Gliffy[/url]

Here’s a summary of the biggest changes:

[list]
[*]I removed as many “abstract” elements that I could. These are elements that are generally not clear to players where they could be found. This includes Carbon, Membrane, Rutile, Zinc, Calcite, Dolomite, Flint, Emery and Calcium, among others.
[*]Loot elements are now put in the world primarily in one and only one place (“coral walls in safe shallows”) to make it clear to players where they must go if they want something. This also means that old areas won’t become obsolete as the player plunges downward. Precious minerals are always found “inside” something else: limestone chunks, sandstone chunks, shale chunks, etc. Anything that’s a chunk can be broken open to find a random mineral inside. Along the same lines, larger lodes of ore will be found inside the terrain in the future.
[*]I removed as many of the intermediate elements as possible. For instance, instead of making “battery acid”, you can use acid mushrooms directly to make batteries.
[*]Each piece of scrap metal can now be refined down into 2 1×1 pieces of titanium. This keeps the inventory/time cost of scrap, but lays the groundwork for “condensing” of materials. 10 1×1 pieces of Titanium can be further crafted into a Titanium ingot, which allows the loot to scale, to allow building of very big things.
[*]I added many more “advanced” intermediate loot ingredients to keep the progression unfolding but also to open up new branches. Wiring kits and computer chips are examples of opening new groups of tech.
[*]Whenever possible, I incorporated more creature loot into the tree. You can make enameled glass from Stalker teeth, Flares from “crash meal” (ewww?), etc. This is an ongoing goal, and a tricky one, but keeping the elements as specific as possible is helping.
[/list]

The [url=http://www.gliffy.com/go/publish/7224075]full tech tree and details can be found here.[/url] This is a live tech tree that I will keep updating for awhile at least).

I hope this explains some of the reasoning that went into some of the sweeping changes! Please let me know what you think here or [url=https://twitter.com/flayra]via Twitter.[/url]

[i]Editors note: This new system will be released to the normal, stable branch in the next major update. We're not sure when that will be just yet, sign up to the [url=http://eepurl.com/8xU4D]dev update mailing list[/url] to be notified when it is live.[/i]

notes.title: Dev Update 8
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Update8Main-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Stasis Rifle, Save & Load, the experimental Terraformer, Bleeders, Bonesharks, and more: A new Subnautica update is available on Steam! Grab a copy of [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/264710/]Subnautica Early Access[/url] to play. Here’s a video that runs through some of the major additions:

http://youtu.be/qMB-0n6tlzk

Tell us what you think about Update 8 here on the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/264710/discussions/]forums[/url], via [url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=356376081]the in-game feedback system[/url], on [url=https://twitter.com/Subnautica/lists/subnautica-dev-team/members]Twitter[/url], and wherever else you can find us!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/StasisRifle-618x348.jpg[/img]

The Stasis Rifle allows you to fire a stasis field, freezing any life form trapped inside. This is pretty useful for getting around dangerous creatures!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Terraformer-618x348.jpg[/img]

The terraformer is an experimental tool that allows you to mess with Subnautica’s voxel terrain. Hold shift and right click to gather material, and then right click to place it almost anywhere you want.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/MainMenu-618x348.jpg[/img]

We’ve rebuilt the guts of the main menu. It still isn’t very pretty, but the rewrite lets us do cool stuff like have a functional news section, and, that’s right, load saved games.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/SaveGame-618x348.jpg[/img]

Subnautica now has save & load functionality. To save, press escape to open the in-game menu, and hit save.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Piping-618x348.jpg[/img]

Pipes can be placed to create a chain of air leading down into the depths. You can use pipes to supply air to keep you breathing underwater for longer…

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/PipingCave-618x348.jpg[/img]

… For example, you could supply air to a cave system!

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Beacon-618x348.jpg[/img]

Craft beacons, and carry them with you while you explore. When you find an interesting place you’d like to revisit, you can deploy a beacon. The beacon will then show up on your hud as a pinger, much like the life pod.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Airbladder-618x348.jpg[/img]

The new Airbladder allows you to control your bouyancy. Activate the air bladder when you want to quickly return to the surface – For air, or perhaps to escape a hostile life form.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Bleeder-618x348.jpg[/img]

There’s a new dangerous life form lurking in the deep. Watch out for bleeders: Get to close, and these critters will suck the blood right out of your arm.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/InventoryImproved-618x348.jpg[/img]

Tweaks under the hood of the inventory system make dumping unwanted loot much easier.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/BoneSharks-618x348.jpg[/img]

Spend some time exploring some of the ocean’s deeper areas, and you’ll probably encounter the new Bone Shark. Just don’t get too close, as like the Stalker, this guy wants to take your head off.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/Compass-618x348.jpg[/img]

Craft a Compass and put it in your inventory to bet a North South East West indicator on your Head Up Display.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/HUDNumerics-618x348.jpg[/img]

Speaking of the HUD, revamped elements now give numerical feedback on health and oxygen status. This also makes it easier to see how much oxygen equipped tanks are providing.

[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2015/01/CurrentGenerator-618x348.jpg[/img]

Building a current generator lets you direct streams of water wherever you want: They’ll push you around, and any creatures caught in the flow too!

As always, this post doesn’t capture everything that went in to the update. Check out the [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]Trello board[/url] and [url=http://subnautica.unknownworlds.com/#/subnautica/checkins]Checkin & Changes list[/url] to see a full smorgasbord of everything that changed between Update’s 7 & Update 8. Sign up to the [url=http://subnauti.us6.list-manage1.com/subscribe?u=bf02bb8619c14d31027c73d97&id=8fa28cd2f4]Subnautica Dev Update mailing list[/url] to get notified when Update 9 is released

notes.title: Update 8 Schedule
notes.content:
[img]http://unknownworlds.com/subnautica/files/2014/12/20150101_SN_UpdateSmall-618x347.jpg[/img]

Predicting the future is very difficult: We leave that job to the [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/282370/]Future Perfect[/url] development team. It is possible, however, to make a decent call about when then next Subnautica development update is going to surface.

We’ve set a rough date of January 15th. We may deliver Update 8 earlier or later than this, but the update will come around that time. The biggest feature we expect to add around that date is save/load. If you’ve been playing in Experimental branch ([url=http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=355026171]See this guide to find out how to get it[/url]) you will have already been able to play around with Jonas’ prototype.

Normally, we want to release a substantial update every two weeks or so. [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/264710/announcements/detail/165837197237037317]Update 7[/url] appeared on December 23rd, which means we’re coming due for another one soon. But it’s the holiday season, and much of the team is taking a break at the moment. That means we are running a little slowly.

Other things that you might see pop up in Update 8 are more creatures, several prototype tools, a tweaked main menu, and an overhauled head-up-display / user-interface. Keep an eye on the [url=https://trello.com/b/yxoJrFgP/subnautica]Subnautica Trello Board[/url] to see how we’re progressing!
